items.title: Variational autoencoder model, encoder, and ELBO
The VAE evidence equals the ELBO plus reverse KL
Dominated pathwise differentiation for VAE training
The fixed-horizon reparameterized variational-training procedure terminates
items.statement:
Under the full input and admissible-domain hypotheses of reparameterized variational training, let $T\ge1$ be its finite integer horizon. For every sequence of its prescribed draws satisfying the stated update-domain requirement, all recorded payoffs $h_t$, gradient vectors $G_t$, and parameter vectors $\eta_t$ are finite. The mathematical procedure completes exactly $T$ rounds and returns the full trajectories $(\eta_0,\ldots,\eta_T)$ and $(h_t,G_t)_{0\le t<T}$, including when one or more noise draws lie in its common null set.

Termination here counts the prescribed draws, branch decisions, pointwise evaluations and vector updates as the operations of the stated mathematical procedure. It asserts neither an implementation or cost bound for arbitrary supplied functions and samplers nor convergence or optimality of the returned parameters.

title: Variational autoencoders and pathwise training — Examples

items.title: A Gaussian model with a positive inference gap and a collapsed latent
items.statement:
Assume AC and use Lebesgue measure for the latent densities. In the first model, a scalar latent variable $Z$ has prior $N(0,4)$, and conditional on $Z=z$ the observation is $X=(Y_1,Y_2)$ with $Y_1,Y_2$ IID $N(z,1)$. At the observed value $x=(2,4)$, the evidence is finite and positive and the posterior is $N(8/3,4/9)$. Restrict the encoder family to $q_m(z\mid x)=N(m,4/9)$ for $m\in[-1,1]$ and choose $m=0$. This encoder is admissible and its reverse-KL gap, with $D_{\rm KL}(q\|\pi):=\int q(z)\log(q(z)/\pi(z))\,dz$, is $D_{\rm KL}(q_0(\cdot\mid x)\|\pi(\cdot\mid x))=8>0$, so its ELBO is exactly $8$ below the log evidence.

In a second model, let $Z\sim N(0,1)$ and use the standard normal density $h(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}$ for $p(x\mid z)=h(x)$, independent of $z$. For every observation $x\in\mathbb R$, the evidence is $0<h(x)<\infty$ and the posterior equals the prior. Choose the constant encoder $q(z\mid x)=N(0,1)$ for every $x$. Its reverse-KL gap is zero and its ELBO equals the log evidence on every fibre. Thus $q(z\mid x)=p_\theta(z\mid x)=p(z)$ for all $x$, a posterior-collapse configuration in which the decoder ignores the latent variable; this is one model configuration, not a claim that VAE training always collapses.
